questions.prompt: You need water. What do you say?
questions.explanation: 물 주세요 means “Water, please.” 주세요 politely asks someone to give you something.

questions.context: You are ready to pay for your drink.
questions.prompt: Ask how much your drink costs.
questions.explanation: 얼마예요? means “How much is it?” 얼마 asks about price. 감사합니다 means “Thank you.”

questions.prompt: You want your drink to go. What do you say?
questions.explanation: 포장해 주세요 asks for takeaway. 여기서 마실게요 means “I will drink it here,” which does not fit leaving the café.

reveal.teachingPoint: 포장 asks for takeaway; 여기서 means here.

questions.prompt: Order your drink without ice. What do you say?
questions.explanation: 얼음 빼 주세요 means “No ice, please.” 빼 주세요 asks to leave something out; 더 주세요 asks for more.

reveal.teachingPoint: 빼 주세요 = leave it out; 더 주세요 = give more

questions.context: You ordered tea, but received coffee.
questions.prompt: Ask to replace the coffee with tea.
questions.explanation: 차로 바꿔 주세요 asks to replace it with tea. 커피로 changes it to coffee; 차 한 잔 더 주세요 asks for an extra cup of tea.

reveal.teachingPoint: 차로 = to tea; 더 asks for more.

questions.context: Your first choice is sold out. No drink is served.
questions.explanation: 로 marks the replacement choice. 도 means “also”; 더 means “more.” Here you are switching your order, not adding another drink.

reveal.teachingPoint: 로 marks the new choice; 도 = also; 더 = more.

questions.suggestedComment: C: 아메리카노로 주세요. = An Americano instead, please. 로 marks the replacement; 도 means also and 더 means more.
